speaker: Joshua

comments.flawless: Joshua: The report was right on the first try. Bonus approved.
comments.done: Joshua: Case closed. Next time, look at the shape of the graph and at what each visitor does before you blame the crowd.

all_clues_monologue: That's enough. Nine thousand devices sent 41,000 requests a minute to one page, with one browser name, and not one of them bought anything.
The sale was real, and it came after. Time to press REPORT and tell the rush from the attack.

email.title: EMAIL > THE SITE, THE SALE, THE CALLS

entries.title: The site is down!
entries.detail:
From: Jonas Pike, web admin
To: IT desk
Time: today 11:58

The site was slow from 11:42 and has been down since 11:50. Everybody says it is Marketing's lunch sale. Can you check?
monologue: The site was slow at 11:42, and the sale starts at 12:00. Eighteen minutes before the sale is a strange time to be crowded.
Is it the sale, or something else?
entries.summary: Jonas says the site was slow from 11:42 and down by 11:50.

entries.title: Lunch sale, 12:00
entries.detail:
From: Leila Haddad, Marketing
To: all customers, all staff
Time: today 09:30

Our lunch sale starts at 12:00 and runs until 13:00. Half price on the best sellers.
monologue: The sale was announced at 09:30 and starts at 12:00. It is real, and it explains a crowd at noon.
Does it explain a crowd at 11:42?
entries.summary: Marketing's lunch sale starts at 12:00, announced at 09:30.

entries.title: Customers cannot buy
entries.detail:
From: Support
To: IT desk
Time: today 12:15

A customer called: the page will not load at the checkout. A second customer says the same. They are real, and they are leaving.
monologue: Real customers cannot get in. Whatever this is, it blocks the people we want.
entries.summary: Real customers could not buy at 12:15.

entries.title: Maintenance window on Sunday
entries.detail:
From: IT desk
To: all staff
Time: Monday

The servers will restart on Sunday at 03:00. It will take about ten minutes.
monologue: A planned restart on Sunday. Not today.
entries.summary: A planned restart is on Sunday at 03:00.

entries.title: Parking permits
entries.detail:
From: Facilities
To: all staff
Time: Tuesday

New permits for the car park are ready at the front desk.
monologue: Parking permits. Nothing here.
entries.summary: New car park permits are at the front desk.

entries.title: /search?q=, 41,000 requests a minute from 11:42
entries.detail:
Time: from 11:42, still going
Page: /search?q=
Requests: 41,000 a minute
Other pages: almost none

Every request asks for the same search page, with the same empty search.
monologue: Forty-one thousand requests a minute, and all of them ask for the same page. A real shopper looks around.
Why would so many people search for nothing?
entries.summary: 41,000 requests a minute, from 11:42, all ask for the same page: /search?q=.

entries.title: 97% of the requests use the browser name bot-kit/1.0
entries.detail:
Time: from 11:42
Browser name: bot-kit/1.0
Share of the requests: 97%
Real browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge

Thousands of different addresses, and all of them call their browser the same made-up name.
monologue: Ninety-seven percent of the requests use one browser name, and it is not a browser anyone uses.
Can thousands of people share one name?
entries.summary: 97% of the requests carry the browser name bot-kit/1.0.

entries.title: Shop and checkout pages, 14,000 requests a minute from 12:05
entries.detail:
Time: from 12:05
Pages: the shop, products, the cart, the checkout
Requests: 14,000 a minute
Browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge

Many pages, real browsers: people shopping.
monologue: This one is big too, but it walks through the whole shop with real browsers. That is how people behave.
entries.summary: The sale brought 14,000 requests a minute from 12:05, to many pages, in real browsers.

entries.title: A search-engine crawler, 30 requests a minute
entries.detail:
Time: every hour
Pages: many, in order
Requests: 30 a minute
Browser name: friendly-bot/2.1

Listed in robots.txt as allowed. It reads politely and slowly.
monologue: A crawler. It is a program, but it is polite, it is listed, and it is slow.
entries.summary: A search-engine crawler reads 30 requests a minute and is allowed.

entries.title: A normal Tuesday: 900 requests a minute
entries.detail:
Time: a normal Tuesday
Pages: many
Requests: 900 a minute
Browsers: real ones

This is what the site looks like on a quiet day.
monologue: 900 requests a minute is the usual. It is the baseline, and it makes 41,000 look as odd as it is.
entries.summary: On a normal Tuesday the site gets 900 requests a minute.

entries.title: Image downloads
entries.detail:
Time: all day
Pages: /images
Requests: 300 a minute

The pictures of the shop, loaded with every page.
monologue: Pictures for the shop. Ordinary.
entries.summary: Image downloads are 300 requests a minute.

entries.title: 9,200 addresses in 40 ranges
entries.detail:
Group: the flood
Addresses: 9,200, in 40 ranges
What they are: cameras, routers and small servers
Owners: nobody here

Devices that were taken over and do what they are told.
monologue: Cameras and routers do not browse for fun. Someone took them over and sends them all at once.
Who controls that many devices?
entries.summary: 9,200 addresses in 40 ranges, mostly cameras and routers, sent the flood.

entries.title: The sale's customers: 3,100 addresses
entries.detail:
Group: the sale's customers
Addresses: 3,100
Where: six countries
What they are: phones and laptops of real people

Different every minute, as people come and go.
monologue: Phones and laptops, in six countries, different every minute. Real people.
entries.summary: The sale's customers are 3,100 addresses, real people in six countries.

entries.title: The office
entries.detail:
Group: the office
Addresses: 40
What they are: staff laptops
monologue: Our own office. A few dozen laptops.
entries.summary: The office is 40 addresses.

entries.title: The partner's API
entries.detail:
Group: the partner's API
Addresses: 2
What they are: the analytics partner's two servers
monologue: The partner's two servers. Known and agreed.
entries.summary: The partner's API is two addresses.

entries.title: Our own monitor
entries.detail:
Group: our own monitor
Addresses: 1
What it does: asks for the shop page 600 times a minute to see whether it is up
Browser name: Our monitor
monologue: Our monitor asks a lot, but it is ours, and it is checking the shop.
entries.summary: Our own monitor asks the shop page 600 times a minute from one address.

login.title: ORDERS > WHO LOGGED IN AND WHO BOUGHT

entries.title: The 9,200 addresses: 0 logins, 0 orders
entries.detail:
Group: the 9,200 addresses of the flood
Logins: 0
Orders: 0
Time: from 11:42

Not one of them has signed in, put anything in a cart or bought anything.
monologue: Not one login and not one order from 9,200 addresses. Real visitors want something.
What do they want, then?
entries.summary: The 9,200 addresses made 0 logins and 0 orders.

entries.title: The sale: 412 orders in 20 minutes
entries.detail:
Group: the sale's customers
Logins: 620
Orders: 412
Time: 12:00 to 12:20

Real people, buying.
monologue: 412 orders in twenty minutes. That is a crowd with money in its hand.
entries.summary: The sale brought 412 orders in 20 minutes.

entries.title: Password resets
entries.detail:
What: password resets
How many: 14 a day
Time: all day
monologue: Fourteen resets a day. Ordinary.
entries.summary: There are about 14 password resets a day.

entries.title: Refunds
entries.detail:
What: refunds
How many: 3 a day
Time: all day
monologue: Three refunds a day. Ordinary.
entries.summary: There are about 3 refunds a day.

entries.title: Newsletter sign-ups
entries.detail:
What: newsletter sign-ups
How many: 21 today
Time: today
monologue: A few newsletter sign-ups. Ordinary.
entries.summary: There were 21 newsletter sign-ups today.

entries.title: Request limit: none
entries.detail:
Setting: the request limit
Where: web-01
Value: none

Nothing stops one visitor from asking as often as it likes.
monologue: No limit at all on web-01. One visitor may ask a million times.
entries.summary: web-01 has no limit on how often one visitor may ask.

entries.title: access.log: 40 MB to 2 GB since 11:42
entries.detail:
Time: from 11:42
Where: web-01
What happened: the log of requests grew from 40 MB to 2 GB in 40 minutes
File: access.log
monologue: The log of requests grew by fifty times in forty minutes. It is full of the same line.
entries.summary: access.log grew from 40 MB to 2 GB in 40 minutes.

entries.title: promo_banner.png
entries.detail:
Time: today 09:20
Where: the shared folder
File: promo_banner.png, 600 KB

Marketing's picture for the sale.
monologue: Marketing's banner. A picture. It has nothing to do with the load.
entries.summary: The sale banner is a 600 KB picture from Marketing.

entries.title: robots.txt
entries.detail:
Where: web-01
File: robots.txt
Content: the search engine's crawler may read the shop, politely
monologue: It says which crawlers may read the shop. The polite crawler is listed.
entries.summary: robots.txt lists which crawlers may read the shop.

entries.title: maintenance.html
entries.detail:
Where: web-01
File: maintenance.html
Content: the page customers see when the site is down for work
monologue: The sorry-we-are-closed page. Not in use today.
entries.summary: maintenance.html is the page shown during planned work.

entries.title: 41,000 requests a minute from 9,200 addresses, from 11:42
entries.detail:
Time: from 11:42
From: 9,200 addresses
Requests: 41,000 a minute
Shape: up in two minutes, then flat

A rush rises, peaks and falls. This one jumped and stayed.
monologue: Up to 41,000 in two minutes, then flat as a table. A crowd of people does not do that.
What makes a flat line?
entries.summary: 41,000 requests a minute from 9,200 addresses began at 11:42.

entries.title: The sale: 14,000 requests a minute from 12:00, peak at 12:20
entries.detail:
Time: from 12:00
From: 3,100 addresses
Requests: up to 14,000 a minute
Shape: rises, peaks at 12:20, then falls

A real rush.
monologue: It rises, peaks at 12:20 and falls. That is the shape of people who came for a sale.
entries.summary: The sale rose from 12:00, peaked at 12:20 with 14,000 requests a minute, then fell.

entries.title: Nightly backup
entries.detail:
Time: every night 01:00
From: backup-01
Sent to: the backup cloud
How much: 9 GB
monologue: The nightly backup. Not today's problem.
entries.summary: The nightly backup copies 9 GB at 01:00.

entries.title: Staff browsing
entries.detail:
Time: all day
From: the office
How much: small
monologue: Staff browsing. Ordinary.
entries.summary: Staff browsing is small.

entries.title: Gateway note: the spike was flagged
entries.detail:
Time: today 11:43
From: the gateway
Note: the gateway flagged the spike of requests as odd at 11:43 and logged it
monologue: The gateway flagged the spike at 11:43, one minute after it began. The note was there to read.
entries.summary: The gateway flagged the spike as odd at 11:43.

entries.title: Gateway note: nothing
entries.detail:
Time: today 11:43
From: the gateway
Note: the gateway let the spike of requests through without a note
monologue: The gateway let the spike through without a note. Nobody was told.
entries.summary: The gateway let the spike through without a note.

entries.title: web-01: processor at 100% since 11:43
entries.detail:
Computer: web-01
Job: the website
Status: overloaded since 11:43
Busy: 100%
Note: the queue of waiting requests is full, so new ones are turned away
monologue: web-01 is at 100% and its queue is full. It cannot take one more visitor, real or not.
What filled it?
entries.summary: web-01 has had its processor at 100% since 11:43, and its queue is full.

entries.title: db-01
entries.detail:
Computer: db-01
Job: the database
Status: running
Busy: 30%
Note: it is not the one under attack
monologue: db-01 is calm. The trouble is at the front door, not the database.
entries.summary: db-01 is running calmly at 30%.

entries.title: The load balancer
entries.detail:
Computer: the load balancer
Job: shares requests between servers
Status: running
Note: it has only one server to send to, web-01
monologue: The balancer has only one server to send requests to. There is nobody to share the load with.
entries.summary: The load balancer has only one server to send to, web-01.

entries.title: Ports: only 80 and 443 are open
entries.detail:
Computer: web-01
Job: what is open to the outside
Note: only ports 80 and 443 are open: the shop and its secure version
monologue: Only the two doors the shop needs are open. Nothing forgotten.
entries.summary: Only ports 80 and 443 are open on web-01.

entries.title: Ports: an old test page on 8081 is open
entries.detail:
Computer: web-01
Job: what is open to the outside
Note: an old test page on port 8081 is open, and the flood is hitting it too
monologue: An old test page on port 8081 is open to the whole world, and the flood is hitting it too.
entries.summary: An old test page on port 8081 is open, and is being hit too.

entries.title: The update server
entries.detail:
Computer: the update server
Job: sends updates to the laptops
Status: running
Busy: 9%
monologue: The update server. Quiet.
entries.summary: The update server is quiet at 9%.

report.solved_explanation: This is a DDoS: so many requests at once that real customers cannot get in. A big crowd is not proof by itself. Look at who is asking and what they do.
